# Interview record · 4.7.1 Owning a Resource

The input of the card as the interview gave it: what the author said, what Claude brought, and where each answer went in the card. It is what the fact check reads the card against.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Card | 4.7.1 Owning a Resource (4 · Data owner and expert, section 4.7 Roles) |
| Author | Enrico, a data colleague (evaluation round of the skill, played by Max) |
| Interviewed | 2026-11-11, with the learning-card skill |
| Fact check | Enrico, the author |
| Test reader | Saskia Bellefroid |

## 1. The reader's question

**Asked:** Who asked you this recently, and how did they put it? Side entrance: nobody asked yet, as the Message is brand new; what do you want an Owner to ask once they get it?

**Answer:** "What do I need to do with this message?", from an owner who has just received "A Resource arrived in your Collection". The author first came with "data arrival" (no topic in the plan; Data Hub calls it Stability), then chose this Message, which names this card (MSG-RES-08, DEC-LR-29). The author answered ahead with the whole procedure: "You are now the proud owner of data, congrats. This comes with the responsibility that you need to represent this data to the organization": describe the data as a whole, describe its fields, define which fields are important, organise it in your Collection with folders if you need them, publish; if the data interests others, they will contact you with questions through the hub, so please reply; later you will be asked to register gaps and usage.

**In the card:** Why now, the quote. The procedure: Core idea, "At Immoscoop", in one sentence.

## 2. What went wrong

**Asked:** What went wrong, concretely? Pushed back: nothing went wrong with the Message yet, so what goes wrong when someone becomes the owner of data without knowing what it means?

**Answer:** "Most Resources stay unpublished for weeks after they arrive", an assumption, as Data Hub is not in use yet. What owners say, expected rather than heard: "I'm not sure it's right, so I don't dare publish it"; "Not sure why I need to do this, I can see the data so it's fine as it is"; "The description is ok"; "Can't be bothered". The author wants the card to stress the why, "make your data available for others to use", then the how, then how the how serves the why.

**In the card:** the situation of Why now (without "weeks", which is not checked); the wrong answers of the first three questions.

## 3. The aha

**Asked:** What is the one thing that, once someone sees it, makes the rest obvious?

**Answer:** "When I publish this properly, others can rely on my data and therefore my work can be used by others", with behind it "the product of your work is your data". In the owner's voice: "I'm proud that what I deliver can be used by others; my domain of expertise can be reused by others because I'm publishing and explaining it properly." The author added that this is a big one for a colleague to grasp quickly. Claude made no suggestion; the compression into one sentence is Claude's.

**In the card:** Core idea, the rule.

## 4. The everyday anchor

**Asked:** Which everyday thing behaves exactly like this?

**Answer:** "You created the perfect meal. You want others to enjoy it, well the quality of your recipe will enable you to pass it on. Take the time to do it properly and one day someone will proudly say: this was my grandmother's recipe." Tested out loud: it carries the work (the meal), what you pass on and its quality (the recipe), who stands behind it (the grandmother's name) and the use far beyond you (one day). Against the fear of question 2, Claude asked what the grandmother does with a recipe she is not sure of: "She writes it down anyway and improves it over time." The author added that the Data Team is there to help, and: "If you don't understand it, as someone owning the domain the data is representing, what are you expecting from your colleagues working on completely different stuff such as accounting or HR or, God forbid, management!"

**In the card:** Core idea, "Like a family recipe", in the author's words; the line on accounting, HR and management closes Why now; the Data Team helps in the Why of the second question.

## 5. Never again, ask first

**Asked:** What may an owner never do again after this card, and what do they ask first from now on?

**Answer:** Never ignore the Message. Ask first "Who needs this besides me?", to which the author added "and how does this person beside me need to interpret this"; Claude wrote it as "Who needs this besides me, and how should they read it?"

**In the card:** You can now, the first question; the ban is the wrong answers "Nothing" and "Wait until someone asks for it" of the first question.

## 6. One card or a family

**Asked:** Is this one card or a small family? The plan called it Owner and steward, and steward is no term of Data Hub.

**Answer:** "Steward out." Both: everything belongs on this card, as a short introduction, a teaser for the cards behind it. The reader understands the why, the how and how the how serves the why, then gets a quick grasp that there is more to come, such as Known Gaps (some data is missing because of …) and intended use (the context you need to understand it). "Ideally they have read this card, seen the next topics and think: damn, indeed it's logical, I also define the gaps and the … and at that point they get eager."

**In the card:** the last sentence of "At Immoscoop" names Known Gaps and intended use; the follow-up cards are on the to-do, as Where to next takes only written cards. The topic is renamed in the plan, from Owner and steward to Owning a Resource.

## 7. Neighbours

**Asked:** Next to which written cards, and which term of the glossary, does this one belong?

**Answer:** K5.1 What a resource is and K5.2 The Level of a Resource; Owner in bold.

**In the card:** Where to next: Deeper K5.2 (from 3 · Confirmed the Owner vouches), Next to it K5.1, and Apply to Collections. The rule bolds **Owner**.

## The ladder

1. **Story:** a cook writes down the recipe of a perfect meal, not sure yet, improves it over time, and years later a grandchild says "this was my grandmother's recipe".
2. **Structure:** a ladder of steps: describe the whole, describe the fields, mark the key fields, put it in a folder, publish; then answer the Questions; later Known Gaps and intended use.
3. **Data Hub:** the Message "A Resource arrived in your Collection", and the page of the Resource, where the Owner describes and publishes it.

The card has no See it: the third rung is a screen of Data Hub, not a chart. Apply leads to Collections instead. The first two rungs are pictures (Figma work); the card has no place for them yet.

## Who brought what

The author brought the reader's question, the misconceptions, the aha, the recipe and its answer to the fear, the line on accounting, HR and management, the ban and the first question, and the shape of a teaser. Claude brought the compression of the aha and of the first question into one sentence each, the four questions of Check your understanding (the fourth, "nobody needs it", is Claude's own trap), the facts of Data Hub behind the example (only the Owner Unit and the Data Team see an unpublished Resource; publishing is the first Confirmation and vouches for what it is, not for every figure; the Business Description stands next to the description of dbt), and the title Owning a Resource. At the quality gate the author confirmed that the card sounds the way the author would explain it, the title, and the fourth question.
